court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
case_name: Surya Vetrikondan vs The State Of Tamilnadu

parties.respondent_defendant: The State Of Tamilnadu, represented by its Chief Secretary, and others

facts_of_case: Petitioner is a lawyer who gave a representation to the Chief Secretary, Government of Tamil Nadu, seeking a scheme for registering all marriages conducted so far and hereinafter.

legal_principles.principle: The solemnization of a marriage must be certified by the officiating priest in the form contained in Schedule II.
legal_principles.held: Every marriage contracted under this Act shall, immediately on the solemnization thereof, be certified by the officiating priest in the form contained in Schedule II.
applicable_acts_sections: Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936 — Section 6

legal_principles.principle: A marriage can be registered under the Special Marriage Act, 1954, if certain conditions are fulfilled.
legal_principles.held: Any marriage celebrated, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, other than a marriage solemnized under the Special Marriage Act, 1872 (3 of 1872), or under this Act, may be registered under this Chapter by a Marriage Officer in the territories to which this Act extends if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:

outcome.final_order: The present writ petition is dismissed.
